how-to-save-money-fast.caption: Example month: seven moves, $105 of it repeats every month.

how-to-start-over-after-budget-failure.alt: A ledger card showing an example restart: $1,640 in checking, less the card, three bills and a cushion, leaving $808 to spend.
how-to-start-over-after-budget-failure.caption: Example: today's balance minus what is still due leaves $808.

end-of-month-money-review.alt: A checklist card with five steps for an end of month review, from writing down every balance to looking at next month's due dates.
end-of-month-money-review.caption: The checks that make up the ten minutes.

how-to-cancel-subscriptions.alt: A script card with three short lines to say when a company pushes back on cancelling: for a discount, for a call-us request, and for chat only.
how-to-cancel-subscriptions.caption: Three short lines for the usual pushbacks.

debt-snowball-vs-avalanche.alt: A table comparing the snowball and avalanche orders for three example debts: same debt-free month, avalanche paying $113.94 less interest.
debt-snowball-vs-avalanche.caption: Example: the two orders finish together, $113.94 apart.

monthly-bills-list.alt: A card showing eight bills added up to $1,891 a month, including three that are not billed monthly.
monthly-bills-list.caption: Example: $223 a month hides in the bills that are not monthly.

organize-your-finances-from-scratch.alt: A checklist of six money areas to write down from memory, with question marks for the gaps.
organize-your-finances-from-scratch.caption: Ten minutes, no statements needed. Mark every gap with a question mark.

split-bills-with-a-partner-or-roommate.alt: A card showing four shared bills and the two thirds share one partner pays, totaling $1,328 of $1,992.
split-bills-with-a-partner-or-roommate.caption: Example: $4,200 and $2,100 take-home gives a 67 and 33 percent split.

subscription-tracker-what-to-track.alt: A small tracker table listing three subscriptions with their renewal dates and a keep, cancel or deciding status.
subscription-tracker-what-to-track.caption: Example: the annual rows are the ones with a decision waiting.

bank-statement-csv-to-budget.alt: A checklist of five things to check in a downloaded bank CSV before importing: header row, sign of spending, amount columns, date order and repeated rows.
bank-statement-csv-to-budget.caption: Five checks to run on any bank CSV before it counts.

financial-binder-what-to-include.alt: A binder page listing six of the seven sections to fill in order: accounts, income, bills, subscriptions, debt and savings goals.
financial-binder-what-to-include.caption: The sections of a working financial binder, in the order to fill them.

sinking-funds-explained.alt: A ledger of five example yearly costs, each divided into a monthly amount, adding up to $175.50 a month to set aside.
sinking-funds-explained.caption: Example: five known costs turned into one monthly figure.

50-30-20-rule-where-it-breaks.alt: A ledger showing $3,500 of after-tax income split into $1,750 for needs, $1,050 for wants and $700 for savings and extra debt payments.
50-30-20-rule-where-it-breaks.caption: Example: the rule applied to $3,500 a month after tax.

budget-for-variable-bills.alt: A ledger of an example electric bill: lowest and highest month, the twelve month total, the average, and the figure to plan toward.
budget-for-variable-bills.caption: Example: twelve bills turned into one planning figure.

credit-card-minimum-payments-how-long.alt: A table of an example $3,000 card at 24 percent showing months to pay off and interest at $90, $140 and $290 a month.
credit-card-minimum-payments-how-long.caption: Example: the same card paid at three monthly amounts.

life-admin-the-work-nobody-teaches-you.alt: A short checklist of what life admin work needs: somewhere for details, how they connect, a quick answer to what's due, help at the moment, and quiet when there's none.
life-admin-the-work-nobody-teaches-you.caption: What this kind of work actually needs, whatever you use to track it.

why-productivity-tools-fail-at-life-admi.alt: A table comparing what task apps assume about work with how life admin actually behaves: connected, already remembered, interrupting, and overwhelming all at once.
why-productivity-tools-fail-at-life-admi.caption: Where a generic task app's assumptions and life admin's reality pull apart.

flight-changed-what-else-is-affected.alt: A table listing a shuttle, hotel check-in, dinner and a next-day tour, each with the one thing to check after a flight moves.
flight-changed-what-else-is-affected.caption: Example: check each booking after the flight, in time order.

flight-delayed-with-a-connection-what-to.alt: A four-step timeline for a delayed flight with a connection: ask a flight attendant, use the app, call from the queue, and ask for one flight.
flight-delayed-with-a-connection-what-to.caption: Example: work the line, the app and the phone at once.

hotel-cannot-find-your-reservation.alt: A checklist of five ways to ask a hotel desk to look up a reservation: confirmation number, booking site reference, payer's name, card digits and dates.
hotel-cannot-find-your-reservation.caption: Try them one at a time, in this order.

organising-a-multi-stop-trip-without-a-s.alt: A table with four bookings on a multi-stop trip, each with a time and the earlier booking it was built on.
organising-a-multi-stop-trip-without-a-s.caption: Example: one line per booking, with what it rests on.

travel-document-checklist.alt: A small table listing each traveler's passport with an expiry date beside the name, and the insurance card, one row per document.
travel-document-checklist.caption: Example: one row per document, with the expiry date beside the name.

how-to-plan-a-group-trip.alt: A table for a group of six listing each booking, who booked it, and which people are on it, including a dinner that one person skips.
how-to-plan-a-group-trip.caption: Example: each booking, who made it, and who is on it.

what-to-keep-on-paper-when-you-travel.alt: A short checklist of what goes on the one printed travel page: local-language address, booking references, insurance, a home contact, passport copies.
what-to-keep-on-paper-when-you-travel.caption: The five things on the page, before you print two copies.

how-to-write-a-one-page-trip-itinerary.alt: A short itinerary table with a time, place and confirmation reference on each line, for a flight, hotel, tram tour and train.
how-to-write-a-one-page-trip-itinerary.caption: Example: one line per booking, with the reference beside it.

packing-list-for-a-week-away.alt: A small table of clothing counts for one adult on a seven day trip: seven pairs of underwear and socks, four tops, two bottoms, two pairs of shoes.
packing-list-for-a-week-away.caption: An example of clothing counts for one adult, mild weather, no laundry.

carry-on-only-packing-list.alt: A checklist of what fits in one carry-on for a week: four tops, two bottoms, five pairs of underwear and socks, one layer, two pairs of shoes, liquids.
carry-on-only-packing-list.caption: An example of counts for one adult and one wash. Check your airline's limits.

packing-and-planning-for-a-trip-with-kid.alt: A checklist for the bag a parent carries when flying with a baby or toddler: spare clothes, diapers and formula, a comfort item, snacks and medicine.
packing-and-planning-for-a-trip-with-kid.caption: An example of what stays with you, not in the checked bag.

lost-passport-wallet-or-phone-abroad-wha.alt: A checklist of what to have ready before calling anyone about a lost passport, wallet or phone: what was lost, who issued it, a contact number, hotel, flight date.
lost-passport-wallet-or-phone-abroad-wha.caption: An example of the details to gather first.

first-international-trip-checklist.alt: A four-step timeline counted back from departure: passports and entry page, visa and insurance, bank and phone plan, then documents in the carry bag.
first-international-trip-checklist.caption: Example: the order to sort a first trip abroad, counted back from departure.

road-trip-planning-checklist.alt: A three-row table of driving days with hours of driving and where you sleep, with a booking reference beside each stay.
road-trip-planning-checklist.caption: Example: one line per driving day, with the hours and a reference beside each stay.

night-before-you-travel-checklist.alt: A short checklist of what goes in the carry bag the night before: ID or passport, cards and cash, phone and charger, medication, and one printed page.
night-before-you-travel-checklist.caption: The carry-bag checks, done the evening before.

what-is-due-on-my-car-right-now.alt: A table of four car jobs with miles and months since each was done, showing which limit decides and one job with no date.
what-is-due-on-my-car-right-now.caption: An example with made-up numbers. Miles or months, whichever comes first.

what-to-tell-a-mechanic-before-work-star.alt: A card with three lines to say at a repair shop: the job you are requesting, a spending limit and a request for written prices.
what-to-tell-a-mechanic-before-work-star.caption: Three sentences to say before the keys change hands. The amounts are examples.

used-car-no-service-records-what-to-do.alt: A five-item checklist for the first week with a used car that has no service records, from asking the seller to starting a log.
used-car-no-service-records-what-to-do.caption: Five steps for a car that came with no paperwork.

car-maintenance-log-what-to-write-down.alt: A sample car maintenance log with three lines, each showing a date, an odometer reading in miles and the work done.
car-maintenance-log-what-to-write-down.caption: An example log. Date, miles and what was done on every line.

selling-your-car-with-a-service-history.alt: A sample service record page with three lines, each showing a date, odometer reading and the work done, oldest first.
selling-your-car-with-a-service-history.caption: An example page. Date, miles and work done, oldest first.

car-maintenance-by-mileage-start-with-yo.alt: A table of typical maintenance intervals by miles and months for oil, brake fluid, coolant and a timing belt, to compare with an owner's manual.
car-maintenance-by-mileage-start-with-yo.caption: Typical example intervals. Your manual has the real ones.

winter-car-prep-checklist.alt: A five-item checklist for winter car prep covering the battery, tires, wipers, coolant and lights, and the emergency kit.
winter-car-prep-checklist.caption: Five checks to finish before the first frost.

two-cars-one-household-maintenance.alt: A table comparing two cars in one household: the sedan is overdue for oil by months while the van has about 1,200 miles left.
two-cars-one-household-maintenance.caption: An example. The car that drives less can be the late one.

glove-box-checklist-what-to-keep.alt: Two checklist cards, one listing what to keep in a glove box such as registration and proof of insurance, and one listing what to leave at home.
glove-box-checklist-what-to-keep.caption: Keep the details in the car and the originals at home.

car-paperwork-dates-organizer.alt: A small table of car registration and insurance dates with an act-by date six weeks earlier, and a note to look six weeks ahead once a month.
car-paperwork-dates-organizer.caption: An example tracker with made-up dates.

first-car-checklist-for-new-drivers.alt: A timeline of the first week with a new car, from calling the insurer to setting up the glove box, and a note to match the VIN in three places.
first-car-checklist-for-new-drivers.caption: The order that keeps the hard-to-fix things first.
